title: The sweep endpoint and a real manifest recompute
status: COMPLETE AS CODE, NOT AS CUSTOMER. Both routes built, tested, CI green, PR open and unmerged. Not deployed, so no live grade exists — and the lane's most important finding is that the recompute, once deployed, will move ZERO cells, for a reason the dispatch did not have.
missionPremise: OPS-16 amendments A-018 and A-019. The statewide serving sweep answers what the product SERVES a human per parcel, which is a different question from the County Manifest's did-a-writer-run, and the two are kept side by side because their disagreement is the finding. The record was FROZEN by the planner at _catalog/parcel_fact_sheet_contract/serving-sweep.ts so the producer (SS-W5 / P-43, hauska-engine) and the consumer (SS-W6 / P-44, hauska-map Command Center) could run in parallel. Nobody was assigned the route between them; the dispatch names that as a planner seam error. Separately the county ledger has no recompute route at all, so the deployed manifest was materialized 2026-08-14T17:41:22.500Z and could only be refreshed by a human running a CLI.
completionPredicate: A stranger can (1) GET /api/serving-sweep from a running cortex-api and receive either a StatewideServingSweep that parses cleanly under Command Center's own parseStatewideSweep, or a NAMED not-ingested state, never an empty envelope; (2) address one county and get its frozen record or a named 404 that cannot be confused with a sweep that found nothing; (3) POST a P-43 artifact with a service token and have it land, with a malformed one rejected listing every problem by path and storing nothing; (4) POST a recompute and receive a fresh computedAt READ BACK FROM THE STORE plus a per-rail delta of what actually moved, with a dry-run proving the freshness fields come from the store rather than from memory. All four hold, exercised over real HTTP against a real Postgres with the actual P-43 artifacts.
scopeBasis: Repo is legacy-design-tools; surface is artifacts/api-server plus the lib/db schema it needs. Deliberately OUT of scope, each for a stated reason rather than by omission: the Command Center panel and the hauska-map proxy POST allowlist (different repo, SS-W6 owns that surface); producing sweep data for the other 252 counties (P-43 work); deploying (planner-owned, and named as the reason no live grade exists); running the recompute against production (a write to live operator-facing state, so it is proposed, not taken); and fixing the swallow inside lib/db's probeRailCapabilities itself, which is guarded at this call site and routed to the planner as a class.

theFindingThatMATTERSMOST.label: VERIFIED by me at source, 2026-08-19, read-only psql against DEPLOYMENT_DATABASE_URL (legacy-design-tools-prod)
theFindingThatMATTERSMOST.headline: A county-ledger recompute run today would move ZERO of 3,556 cells. The 4-day-old snapshot is cell-for-cell identical to what a fresh compute produces.
theFindingThatMATTERSMOST.andTheFootprintPart: county_facet_coverage holds ZERO rows for facet 'footprint'. All 254 footprint cells read not-yet before a recompute and would read not-yet after one. The ledger reports footprint as not-yet because nothing has SCORED footprint, not because the snapshot is stale.
theFindingThatMATTERSMOST.correctionToTheDispatch: The dispatch says the ledger reports footprint as not-yet 'because it was computed 67 hours earlier'. The staleness is real as a timestamp and is not the cause. This is the successful-outcome case DEV_PROCESS 3.2 describes: a planner figure reported wrong.

A 254-county statewide body does NOT fit and must be posted county by county. Stated in the route doc where it is read.

routesDelivered.concurrency: withClusterSweepLock advisory lock; a contender gets 409 recompute_in_progress, never a second heavy scan
routesDelivered.timeouts: statement_timeout 240s inside the transaction, under Cloud Run's 300s request timeout (--timeout=300, verified in the deploy workflow)
routesDelivered.reports: computedAt (moves every call by construction), store.computedAtBefore and store.computedAtAfter (both read from county_ledger_snapshot, the second on a fresh read after commit), store.computedAtMovedInStore, store.persistedAsComputed, store.stalenessBeforeMs, and delta (payloadChanged, summaryChanges, cells.{before,after,changed,added,removed,byRailKey})
routesDelivered.failsClosed: 500 recompute_not_persisted when applied and the store does not carry the computed timestamp

routesDelivered.why: a named tombstone, NOT a second name for the recompute. Unmatched GET /api/* falls through to the SPA catch-all and answers HTML 200, which reads as served — the same fallthrough that made this lane's missing route look like a data problem.

howARecomputeIsTriggeredAndByWhom.today: Any holder of the cortex-api SERVICE_API_KEY: `curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $SERVICE_API_KEY" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' https://cortex-api-tds7av26va-uc.a.run.app/api/county-ledger/recompute`. The -d '{}' is not optional: a bodyless POST is rejected by the Cloud Run frontend with 411 before Express sees it, and 411 says nothing about whether the route exists.
howARecomputeIsTriggeredAndByWhom.intendedProducerSeam: hauska-engine's scorers call it after scoring, the same shape as POST /api/onboarding-ledger/ingest. The existing countyLedgerMaterializeCli --apply remains valid and is the fallback when a compute would exceed the request timeout.
howARecomputeIsTriggeredAndByWhom.fromCommandCenter: NOT POSSIBLE without a change in another repo. The console reaches cortex-api through hauska-map's Vercel proxy (api/spine.ts), which allowlists POST paths explicitly and defaults to GET/HEAD only; /api/county-ledger/recompute is not on that list. The GET routes need no proxy change and will work as soon as this is deployed.
howARecomputeIsTriggeredAndByWhom.afterDeploy: the recompute should be run once, and its `delta` read rather than its `computedAt`. Per the finding above the expected delta is all-zero; that is the correct result and must not be reported as a failure OR as a refresh.

defectsFoundAndFixed.finding: probeRailCapabilities swallows a failed COUNT DISTINCT per rail and returns null with a limitation string. Local on a pooled connection; NOT local inside a transaction, where the first failing probe aborts everything after it — including the snapshot write — with an error naming only the write.
defectsFoundAndFixed.reachable: the mud probe reads tx_special_district (lib/db/src/railCoverageCapability.ts:145), which is not in the drizzle schema and so exists in no test schema and no fresh database. Reproduced: the first recompute integration test failed with 'current transaction is aborted, commands ignored until end of transaction block'.
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: each capability probe runs in its own SAVEPOINT, and computeCountyLedgerPayload gained an explicit capabilityDb option so the guard is visible at the call site.
defectsFoundAndFixed.stillOpen: the swallow in lib/db is untouched. Any FUTURE caller wrapping this compute in a transaction inherits the same trap.

defectsFoundAndFixed.finding: the payload diff compared JSON.stringify output. The BEFORE payload comes out of a jsonb column and the AFTER payload is a fresh JS object; jsonb does not preserve key order, so two identical recomputes reported EVERY cell as changed.
defectsFoundAndFixed.howCaught: the test asserting a BORING result — 'a second recompute with nothing changed reports an all-zero delta, not a win'. A suite that only asserted interesting outcomes ships this.
defectsFoundAndFixed.fix: key-sorted comparison with the reason recorded at the function.

backlogItemsForThePlanner: probeRailCapabilities swallows per-probe errors in lib/db. Guarded at this call site with a SAVEPOINT; the swallow itself is unchanged, so the next transactional caller inherits the trap. Either make the helper savepoint-aware or make it declare that it must not run inside a transaction.

tx_special_district is read by the mud capability probe and is not part of the drizzle schema, so it is absent from every test schema and every fresh database and its probe errors on each run. Either add it to the schema or make the probe check to_regclass first.
county_facet_coverage carries BOTH 'land-use' (19 rows) and 'landuse' (254 rows) as facet strings. One subject, two keys, in the table the ledger reads. Worth a ruling.

Six of fourteen rails have never been scored at all: footprint, roads, easement, rrc-wells, rrc-pipelines, rail-corridor. Their county_rail rows nonetheless declare has_writer=true, which is the hand-declared-drift class already on record.

The frozen serving-sweep record now has THREE copies: the planner's, Command Center's mirror, and this repo's validator. There is no automated divergence test across repos because they are three repositories. This is the CTRL-1 shape and it is not mitigated, only stated.
hauska-map's api/spine.ts must allowlist POST /api/county-ledger/recompute before the console can trigger a recompute. The GET sweep routes need no proxy change.
whatRemainsOPEN: NOT DEPLOYED. Code-done is not customer-done; there is no live grade and this lane does not claim one. The Command Center panel will keep rendering its honest not-served state until cortex-api is deployed from this branch.
PR 437 is open and unmerged by lane rule, CI green on head 12691f4c.

No sweep data is ingested anywhere. The store ships empty and the endpoint will answer 503 serving_sweep_not_ingested until a producer posts. The two P-43 counties can be loaded with one curl of _catalog/serving_sweep_2026-08-18/statewide.json once deployed.

The recompute has never run against production. Expected result when it does: computedAt moves, delta is all-zero, and footprint stays not-yet on all 254 cells. That is the honest outcome, not a failure and not a refresh.

The claim 'whatever this endpoint serves parses cleanly under Command Center's parser' is enforced by mirroring its rules and asserting them here; it is NOT proven end to end, because the console's parser lives in another repo and cannot be imported.
The 100kb express.json body cap means a 254-county statewide ingest must be posted county by county. Measured against the two real artifacts, not assumed, and stated at the route.
